title: SonicWall researchers say fake Minecraft mod library steals session tokens, per Cyber Security News
date_note: Cyber Security News page gives only its publication day; the SonicWall original was not found or read.
summary: Cyber Security News, relaying SonicWall Capture Labs research, reports a Java file named Farmutils-Loader.jar disguised as a Fabric mod library. It reads the player's username, account ID and Minecraft services access token, finds its command server through a Polygon smart contract, and fetches a second stage disguised as a PNG. SonicWall did not recover that second stage, so its targets are unconfirmed.
plain: A fake Minecraft mod file can take a player's game session token and fetch more malware. The security firm could not recover the second stage, so its goals are unconfirmed.
exec: Gamers who run the fake mod file can lose their Minecraft session token; the second-stage payload was not recovered, so its aims are unconfirmed.
action: Cyber Security News advises disconnecting the Windows device if the file was launched, running a full scan, reviewing account activity from a clean device, and downloading mods only from official or trusted platforms.
impact: Minecraft session token theft and possible further malware on Windows PCs that run the file.

validation.note: Only Cyber Security News was read; the SonicWall original could not be found.

review.note: Compared file name, data read, Polygon lookup, PNG second stage, unrecovered stage and advice against Cyber Security News
